On February 11, 2025, at 3:05 AM UTC, the production server in us-east-1 experienced a downtime where all customer-facing APIs were returning 503 errors. Dave Wilson reported that CPU usage spiked to 100% and database connections were exhausted [Email 2].

Bob Martinez identified an issue with a new batch job deployed on Friday which had a connection leak, opening 50 connections per run without releasing them [Email 3]. The application server was restarted, the pool limit increased to 200, and API responses resumed. A fix for the connection leak was pushed to staging for review [Email 4].

Dave Wilson confirmed that the issue stemmed from a missing finally block in the database client of the nightly analytics batch job deployed on February 7th [Email 4]. The proper fix was merged into production at 14:30 UTC, and additional monitoring was put in place to alert when connection pools reach 80% capacity [Email 5].

The incident caused a full outage for 45 minutes with an additional degraded period of about 12 minutes. A postmortem document is available at https://wiki.acme.com/postmortem/2025-02-11 [Email 5].
